title: Build support, trust, and recovery knowledge for internal visual product, design, diagram, and proposal workspace
summary: Make common questions, failure states, recovery, diagnostics, privacy, and support expectations understandable for `internal visual product, design, diagram, and proposal workspace`.
acceptance_criteria: Build a support and trust model for `internal visual product, design, diagram, and proposal workspace` centered on `open repository-backed design truth, place screens and diagram objects, select and transform them, connect flows, inspect source context, and save`.
Inventory likely user questions, setup problems, data issues, errors, external blockers, and recovery needs.
Provide concise in-product help at the point of need rather than only a large external manual.
Define known-issue, outage, stale-data, hardware, billing, permission, and unsupported-state communication where relevant.
Provide safe export of version, configuration, evidence, and redacted diagnostics.
Preview every support bundle field and exclude credentials and unnecessary private data.
Define support severity, triage, owner, response posture, and escalation.
Separate product defect, misunderstanding, external service, device or hardware, account, billing, data, and feature request.
Connect support evidence to repository revision, release, ticket, and finding.
Provide recovery or next action for every known failure state.
Document backup, restore, correction, deletion, entitlement, billing, or migration support where applicable.
Provide accessible and localized support content.
Keep support content versioned and mark stale advice.
Provide a privacy and retention policy for support evidence.
Allow the user to withdraw or delete optional support attachments where possible.
Create repeatable fixtures for common support scenarios.
Feed validated recurring issues into proposed findings without auto-prioritizing by volume alone.
Measure support burden and time-to-resolution without recording unrelated user behavior.
Define sunset and archive behavior for obsolete versions.
Do not imply human support availability that does not exist.
Verify support flows and redaction.
Finish with zero app-owned warnings.

agent_notes: Portfolio Human Validation & Product Launch Wave 13.
Non-scope: do not release, deploy, sign, publish, enable billing or ads, operate hardware, write NAS data, migrate users, merge products, or create future game repositories.
Alternative considered and rejected: relying on internal confidence, green builds, or download counts without observed user or operator value would create false product certainty.
Research, telemetry, and feedback must remain privacy-safe, versioned, and optional where the product role requires it.
